page: UpCloud GPU-48xCPU-480GB-2xB200 is a GPU-accelerated server designed for intensive computational workloads. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8570 processor with 48 physical cores and 48 vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 480.0 GB of system memory, providing 10.0 GB of RAM per core. Crucially, the server integrates two NVIDIA Blackwell B200 GPUs with a combined VRAM of 384 GB. Local storage is not bundled with this instance type.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong multi-core capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU scores reaching the top 25% and top 10% tiers respectively. The system demonstrates exceptional memory bandwidth, particularly in large-block read operations, which rank in the top 10%. In data processing tasks, the server achieves top-tier results in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and PassMark database operations. For language model workloads, prompt processing with a small 135M model reaches top-tier speeds of 9458.91 tokens per second.

From a resource density perspective, the combination of massive system memory and dual Blackwell GPUs offers high qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring substantial parallel processing power without local storage dependencies. The lack of local storage represents a key architectural tradeoff, requiring external network storage solutions. This server is highly suited for large-scale LLM inference, deep learning training, complex database operations, and high-throughput data processing.
description: UpCloud GPU-48xCPU-480GB-2xB200 is a high-capacity GPU-accelerated server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 48 Intel Xeon 8570 vCPUs, 480.0 GB of system memory, and two NVIDIA Blackwell B200 GPUs delivering 384 GB of total VRAM. Local storage is omitted from this configuration. Benchmark data highlights top-tier performance in multi-core processing, large-block memory read bandwidth, and database operations. The server also excels in LLM prompt processing, achieving 9458.91 tokens per second on small models. Given its massive memory footprint and dual-GPU architecture, this instance is optimized for deep learning, large-scale AI inference, and intensive database workloads.
